marrow__PHYS_CH16_Q019.takeaway: Mossy fibers and granule-cell parallel fibers are both excitatory pathways.
marrow__PHYS_CH16_Q019.displayText: Cerebellar excitatory inputs include mossy fibers, climbing fibers, and granule-cell parallel fibers. Mossy fibers excite granule cells; granule axons bifurcate in the molecular layer as parallel fibers and excite many Purkinje cells. Climbing fibers strongly excite individual Purkinje cells; basket, stellate, and Golgi cells are inhibitory interneurons.

rationales.a: Mossy fibers excite the cerebellar circuit, but Purkinje output to deep nuclei is inhibitory, so this pair is not both excitatory.
rationales.b: Climbing fibers are excitatory, whereas Golgi cells are inhibitory interneurons.
rationales.d: Climbing fibers excite Purkinje cells, but basket cells inhibit them.

marrow__PHYS_CH16_Q020.takeaway: Stellate-cell inhibition of Purkinje cells is feedforward inhibition.
marrow__PHYS_CH16_Q020.displayText: Parallel fibers excite stellate and basket interneurons, which then inhibit Purkinje cells. Because the inhibitory interneuron is activated by the same incoming pathway before suppressing its target, this is feedforward inhibition; Renshaw-cell suppression of the neuron that activated it is feedback inhibition.

rationales.a: Presynaptic inhibition acts at a transmitter terminal before synaptic release; stellate cells inhibit Purkinje-cell bodies/dendrites postsynaptically.
rationales.b: Feedback inhibition is exemplified by Renshaw circuits; here parallel-fiber input recruits stellate cells ahead of Purkinje output.
rationales.d: Stellate cells do inhibit Purkinje cells, as part of cerebellar feedforward control.
